correctness.rationale: Identify a Johnson vertex with a base edge; inclusive closed neighborhood of base edge e intersects query support S in precisely the edges meeting e. An empty trace forces two distinct isolated base vertices. A singleton trace for each support edge forces at least one endpoint of every support edge to be degree one, hence every nontrivial connected support component is a star. The full trace needs no more than two components. To realize a three-edge subset but omit another in one star forces star size <=3, and with two components each size <=2. Conversely choose two base endpoint representatives: star centers for full component, leaves for singleton/two selected edges, isolated vertices for omissions. This realizes all traces for exactly the classified shapes. Counting one-star and two-star cases yields coefficients s_1=1[n>=4] C(n,2), s_2=1[n>=5] n C(n-1,2)+1[n>=6]3C(n,4), s_3=1[n>=6]nC(n-1,3)+1[n>=7]nC(n-1,2)C(n-3,2), s_4=1[n>=8]C(n,2)C(n-2,2)C(n-4,2), zero for k>4. The exceptional n=2,3 cases and all cutoffs are covered. Literal independent enumeration verifies every size-<=4 support for n=2..8; upper bound for arbitrary sizes follows from proof, not enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Adler et al's Theorem 3.7 gives a general four-point open VC bound; its Corollary treats boundedness of boolean combinations including closed sets, not enumeration. Coudert et al's general closed-VC algorithm does not state these motif counts. The closed Johnson-three theorem concerns triples and cannot determine the pair-edge census.

value.rationale: Natural complete classification of the shattered-support complex of a highly symmetric graph family, with all support-size counts, sharp ambient-size cutoffs and a structural characterization useful for learning-theoretic sample complexity and motif counting. It is not a mere new proof of the known VC dimension: all lower coefficients and the closed/open threshold shift are additional precise invariants.

limitations: Applies only to closed radius-one neighborhoods in J(n,2), not open or arbitrary Johnson rank.
